blocks.content: The Constitution envisions the UPSC to be the watchdog of merit system in India.

rows: Ineligible for any employment under GoI or State
Eligible as Chairman of UPSC or SPSC only

items: Recommendations made by the UPSC are advisory in nature and not binding on the executive, though reasons for non-acceptance must be laid before Parliament.
The Supreme Court's advice given during an inquiry regarding removal on grounds of misbehaviour is legally binding on the President.
The Chairman of UPSC is strictly ineligible for any further employment under the Government of India or any State Government after demitting office.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is the central recruiting agency in India, established under Article 315 of Part XIV of the Constitution.
The Chairman and other members of UPSC are appointed by the President of India for a term of 6 years or until reaching 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
The Chairman and members can be removed by the President on grounds of misbehaviour only after an inquiry conducted by the Supreme Court.
All administrative expenses, including salaries, allowances, and pensions of the Chairman and members, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
UPSC acts as the watchdog of the merit system in India, conducting competitive examinations for recruitment to All-India Services and Central Services.
